basic_information.name: R2R (Reason to Retrieve) by SciPhi
basic_information.creator: SciPhi AI, founded by Owen Colegrove (CEO, PhD in particle physics from UC Santa Barbara, former quantitative strategist at Citadel). Y Combinator-backed (W24 batch).
basic_information.description: R2R is an open-source, production-ready agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework built around a RESTful API. It provides an all-in-one solution for multimodal content ingestion (text, PDF, JSON, images, audio), hybrid search combining semantic and keyword retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion, configurable GraphRAG with automatic entity and relationship extraction, and comprehensive user/document management with authentication and collections-based multitenancy. Its Deep Research API enables multi-step reasoning that fetches and synthesizes data from internal knowledge bases and the web. SciPhi also created Triplex, a state-of-the-art open-source model for knowledge graph construction that outperforms GPT-4 at 1/60th the cost. SciPhi Cloud offers managed deployment with a free tier, while the self-hosted version is fully open source.
basic_information.release_date: February 2024 (initial launch on Hacker News); actively maintained with frequent releases through 2025-2026. Latest PyPI version: 3.2.35+.
basic_information.license: Open-core model. The core R2R engine is open source (MIT license per GitHub). SciPhi Cloud adds proprietary enterprise features (advanced graph analytics, custom extraction rules, dedicated support). Triplex model weights are cc-by-nc-sa-4.0, waived for organizations under $5M revenue.
basic_information.github_stars: ~7,700 (as of February 2026, github.com/SciPhi-AI/R2R — 7,193-7,668 range across sources, 585+ forks, 37 contributors, 1,033+ commits)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Server-based (containerized RESTful API). Core architecture built on PostgreSQL with pgvector for vector storage and full-text search, Hatchet (RabbitMQ-based) for workflow orchestration, and optional Unstructured.io integration for advanced document parsing. Deployable as a lightweight single-service or full Docker Compose stack with all infrastructure components.
technical_architecture.language: Python (core engine and SDK — pip install r2r), TypeScript/JavaScript (r2r-js client SDK, R2R-Application dashboard built with React + Next.js)
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports any embedding dimension via configurable embedding providers. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, local models (via LiteLLM gateway), and custom embedding endpoints. No hard dimension limit — constrained only by pgvector backend capabilities.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: HNSW indexing via pgvector extension in PostgreSQL. Full-text search uses PostgreSQL ts_rank and websearch_to_tsquery for keyword retrieval. Hybrid search combines vector similarity and full-text search results via reciprocal rank fusion. Knowledge graph indexing stores entities, relationships, and communities in PostgreSQL.
technical_architecture.scalability: PostgreSQL-backed storage scales with standard database scaling patterns (vertical scaling, read replicas, connection pooling). Hatchet orchestration enables distributed workflow processing. Collections system supports multitenancy with per-user and per-group document partitioning. S3 file provider support introduced as alternative to PostgreSQL Large Objects for large-scale document storage. Designed for production workloads — demonstrated throughput of 160,000+ tokens per second in benchmarks.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted via pip install (lightweight), Docker Compose (full-featured with Hatchet orchestration + Unstructured.io), Kubernetes. SciPhi Cloud managed service with one-click deployment, auto-scaling, and no infrastructure management. Cloud app available at app.sciphi.ai with free tier (no credit card required).

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval (semantic similarity via pgvector), sparse keyword retrieval (PostgreSQL full-text search with BM25-style ranking), hybrid search (combining dense + sparse with reciprocal rank fusion for enhanced relevancy), knowledge graph retrieval (entity and relationship queries, community detection), web search integration (via Serper or Google APIs for live external data), agentic retrieval (Deep Research agent with multi-step reasoning that dynamically selects retrieval strategies).
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Recursive chunking method with configurable chunk size (default 1,024 characters) and chunk overlap (default 512 characters). Lite deployment uses built-in R2R parser; full deployment integrates Unstructured.io for structure-aware parsing of complex documents (supports 27+ file types including PDFs with embedded tables, images, and complex layouts). Document-structure-aware parsing available through Unstructured integration.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion for score fusion across semantic and keyword results. Supports applying reranking to search results. Specific cross-encoder or ColBERT reranking integrations available through configuration. [uncertain]
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Native multimodal ingestion supporting .txt, .pdf, .json, .png, .mp3, and more. Full deployment with Unstructured.io extends this to 27+ file types including complex PDFs with embedded images and tables. Audio file processing supported. Image and document parsing for knowledge extraction.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: First-class GraphRAG support — automatically extracts entities and relationships from documents to build knowledge graphs. Collection-based graph architecture with entity management (add, update, retrieve), relationship management (create, query), and community detection. Customizable extraction prompts and model configurations (kg_triples_extraction_prompt). SciPhi developed Triplex, a specialized 3.8B-parameter model (fine-tuned Phi-3) for knowledge graph construction that achieves GPT-4-level quality at 1/60th the cost. Triplex is integrated natively with R2R for local graph building.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in citation and source attribution — RAG responses include structured citation objects linking specific passages to their source documents. Source citation and evidence-based responses are a core feature of the RAG mode. Deep Research agent provides sourced, citation-backed answers with autonomous web scraping capabilities for verification.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Agentic RAG with multi-step reasoning through Deep Research API — the agent iteratively fetches relevant data, synthesizes across multiple retrieval steps, and composes comprehensive answers. Supports streaming partial output (RAWR) for long answers. Agent tools include local_search (chunks + knowledge graph), content (full document retrieval), and web_search (live external data), allowing dynamic context assembly. [uncertain]

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: No published p50/p99 latency figures. End-to-end latency depends on chosen LLM provider, embedding model, and document collection size. RESTful API architecture adds minimal overhead. Streaming output (RAWR) improves perceived latency for complex queries. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: R2R demonstrated the highest throughput among tested RAG frameworks, processing a benchmark dataset in 62.97 seconds, translating to over 160,000 tokens per second. This was measured in a comparative benchmark against LlamaIndex, Haystack, LangChain, and RAGFlow.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: No standardized public accuracy metrics (faithfulness, relevance scores) published. RAG responses grounded in retrieved content with built-in citation tracking. Knowledge graph integration improves retrieval precision for entity-centric queries. Evaluation depends on configuration choices (embedding model, chunking, reranking). [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: SciPhi published a comparative benchmark (sciphi.ai/blog/benchmarking) showing R2R outperforming LlamaIndex, Haystack, LangChain, and RAGFlow on throughput. Triplex model benchmarked against GPT-4 for knowledge graph construction, achieving comparable or better quality at 98% cost reduction. No MTEB, BEIR, or ANN-Benchmarks results (R2R is a framework, not an embedding model or vector DB). [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: R2R is positioned as a higher-level production framework — described as 'what NextJS is to React' relative to LangChain/LlamaIndex. Pipelines are fully customizable and can incorporate custom logic from LangChain or LlamaIndex. Not a plug-in to other orchestrators but rather a standalone production system that can coexist with them. Competes with LlamaIndex, Haystack, LangChain, and RAGFlow as an alternative all-in-one solution.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o, etc.), Anthropic (Claude family, including extended thinking support), Azure Foundry models. LiteLLM integration extends compatibility to 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format. Supports local LLMs via vLLM, HuggingFace, and Ollama. Embedding providers similarly flexible through LiteLLM gateway.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes — R2R provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that enables Claude and other MCP-compatible models to search through knowledge bases, perform vector searches, graph searches, web searches, and document searches. Official MCP cookbook in documentation. Third-party R2R MCP server also available at mcp.so.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: File-based ingestion via API: .txt, .pdf, .json, .png, .mp3, .csv, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx, and more (27+ types with Unstructured.io). S3 file provider support for cloud storage. Web crawling with autonomous scraping capabilities. Direct API ingestion for programmatic data loading. No native Confluence, Notion, or Slack connectors (data sources requested as GitHub Issue #204 — not yet built-in as of early 2026). [uncertain]
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Comprehensive monitoring through SciPhi Cloud dashboard with insights and analytics. Self-hosted deployments have API-level logging and configuration options. No confirmed OpenTelemetry, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix, or Langfuse native integrations found in documentation. LiteLLM integration may provide some OpenTelemetry passthrough. [uncertain]

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core: self-hosted R2R is free (you pay only infrastructure costs). SciPhi Cloud charges a flat fee per request, with two request types: document indexation and generation. Free tier available with no credit card required. Enterprise plans for advanced features and scale with custom pricing.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Self-hosted: completely free, unlimited use (MIT license). SciPhi Cloud: generous free tier at app.sciphi.ai (no credit card required) — sufficient for prototyping and small projects. Exact free tier limits not publicly documented.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Self-hosted costs are infrastructure-only: PostgreSQL hosting ($20-200+/month depending on scale), compute for R2R server and Hatchet orchestration, LLM API costs (passed through to providers). SciPhi Cloud enterprise pricing is custom — contact sales. Triplex model enables knowledge graph construction at 1/60th the cost of GPT-4, significantly reducing GraphRAG costs. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted POC: near-zero (local Docker Compose + OpenAI API key). Self-hosted production: PostgreSQL ($50-500+/month), compute ($100-500+/month for server + orchestration), LLM API costs ($50-500+/month depending on volume), embedding costs ($10-50+/month). SciPhi Cloud: flat per-request pricing eliminates infrastructure management costs. Total POC: <$50/month; production: $200-2,000+/month depending on scale and LLM usage. [uncertain]

adoption_and_market.market_position: Emerging/challenger in the RAG framework space. R2R is a newer entrant (Feb 2024) positioning itself as the most advanced production-ready RAG system, competing directly with established frameworks like LlamaIndex (~47K stars), LangChain (~100K stars), and Haystack. Key differentiator: all-in-one production platform with built-in GraphRAG, hybrid search, user management, and Deep Research agents — versus component libraries that require assembly. Growing rapidly but smaller community than incumbents.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: KindredPM (went from zero to revenue-generating startup in 5 months using R2R as core infrastructure). Robovision (AI company using R2R for advanced retrieval). HybridRAG enterprise customers (testimonials about accurate, context-rich answers). SciPhi states it is 'trusted by enterprises' but specific Fortune 500 names not publicly disclosed. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: ~7,700 stars, 585+ forks, 37 contributors, 1,033+ commits (SciPhi-AI/R2R). R2R-Application (React/Next.js dashboard) is a separate repository. PyPI package available as 'r2r'. Active Product Hunt presence with launch announcements. Discord/Slack community size not publicly reported. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Y Combinator W24 batch. Pre-seed: $500K from Y Combinator (April 2024, per Tracxn). Crunchbase profile exists but detailed funding beyond YC standard deal not publicly confirmed. Owen Colegrove is a second-time founder with Citadel quant background. Valuation not publicly disclosed. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Primary competitors: LlamaIndex (largest RAG-specific framework, ~47K stars, $27.5M funding), LangChain (broadest orchestration framework, ~100K stars), Haystack by deepset (opinionated pipeline design), RAGFlow by InfiniFlow (deep document understanding focus), Verba by Weaviate (user-friendly RAG interface). R2R differentiators: (1) built-in GraphRAG with Triplex model, (2) all-in-one production system vs component library, (3) Deep Research agent with multi-step reasoning, (4) PostgreSQL-native architecture (single database for vectors, full-text, graphs, and user management), (5) highest throughput in comparative benchmarks.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best fit for startups needing a production-ready RAG backend quickly without assembling separate components (vector DB + orchestrator + auth + graph DB). Ideal team size: 1-5 engineers who want to deploy RAG without deep infrastructure expertise. Budget: free self-hosted with infrastructure costs starting around $50-200/month for production. Use case fit: knowledge bases with complex entity relationships (legal, healthcare, finance), document-intensive products where GraphRAG adds value, products requiring user authentication and document-level access control. The 'deploy in 5 lines of code' pitch makes it attractive for hackathons and MVPs. Not ideal for: teams needing maximum ecosystem flexibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex have 10x more integrations), or teams already invested in another framework.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Self-host R2R when: team wants full control over data and infrastructure, cost sensitivity at scale, need deep customization of retrieval pipeline, strict data residency requirements. Use SciPhi Cloud when: speed-to-market is critical, team is small (1-3 engineers), want to avoid managing PostgreSQL + Hatchet + Unstructured infrastructure, need enterprise support and SLA. Key tradeoff: SciPhi Cloud removes operational burden but locks you into their platform; self-hosted is free but requires DevOps capacity for Docker/Kubernetes management.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC/demo: hours to 1 day (pip install r2r, set OpenAI API key, run server — '5 lines of code' claim). MVP with hybrid search and user auth: 1-2 weeks. Production with GraphRAG, Deep Research, and monitoring: 3-6 weeks. SciPhi Cloud deployment: 1-3 days for basic setup, 2-4 weeks for full production configuration. Docker Compose full deployment with Hatchet + Unstructured: 1-2 days initial setup.
key_lessons: R2R's PostgreSQL-native architecture is a strategic advantage for startups — it means one database handles vectors, full-text search, knowledge graphs, user management, and document storage, reducing operational complexity compared to running separate Pinecone + Neo4j + Auth0 services.

GraphRAG is R2R's strongest differentiator — if your use case involves entity-rich documents (contracts, medical records, legal filings) where relationships between entities matter, R2R's built-in knowledge graph with Triplex model provides significant value that competitors require multiple add-ons to match.

The Triplex model (98% cost reduction vs GPT-4 for graph construction) is a compelling example of how smaller, specialized models can outperform general-purpose LLMs for specific tasks — a lesson applicable beyond RAG to any AI product strategy.

R2R's smaller ecosystem (37 contributors, ~7.7K stars) compared to LangChain/LlamaIndex means less community support, fewer tutorials, and higher risk of breaking changes — startups should weigh the 'all-in-one convenience' against the 'ecosystem depth' when choosing.

The Deep Research agent pattern (iterative retrieval + reasoning + web search) represents the emerging agentic RAG paradigm — startups building with R2R get exposure to this architecture, which is becoming the standard for production RAG in 2025-2026.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Partial — SciPhi Cloud provides a web dashboard (app.sciphi.ai) for managing documents, collections, and users. The R2R-Application is an open-source React + Next.js dashboard for interacting with R2R deployments. However, these are management interfaces, not visual no-code pipeline builders. Pipeline configuration is done through TOML config files and API calls, not drag-and-drop.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — SciPhi Cloud dashboard demo, RAG pipeline configuration), Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — R2R as Build vs Buy case study, PostgreSQL-native architecture decisions, GraphRAG vs simple RAG tradeoffs), Session 4 (AI business models — open-core model analysis, YC-backed startup case study, Triplex model as specialized AI strategy)

confidence.data_quality: Medium-High — information sourced from official R2R documentation (r2r-docs.sciphi.ai), GitHub repository (SciPhi-AI/R2R), Y Combinator company page, Tracxn funding data, SciPhi blog posts, Product Hunt launches, PyPI package registry, Hacker News launch thread, and multiple independent RAG framework comparison articles. Pricing details are limited as SciPhi Cloud specific tiers are not publicly documented.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub statistics confirmed across multiple sources (GitHub itself, tom-doerr.github.io showcase, bestofai.com). YC backing confirmed by ycombinator.com/companies/sciphi. Funding amount ($500K) confirmed by Tracxn. Triplex model capabilities confirmed by HuggingFace model card and SciPhi blog. Throughput benchmark confirmed by SciPhi's own blog (sciphi.ai/blog/benchmarking). Customer testimonials from sciphi.ai website.
confidence.caveats: R2R is a rapidly evolving project — features and architecture may change significantly between versions. The throughput benchmark (160K tokens/sec) is from SciPhi's own comparative study, not an independent third-party evaluation. Customer testimonials are self-reported on the company website. SciPhi Cloud pricing details are not publicly documented — may change. The project has a relatively small contributor base (37 contributors) compared to established frameworks, which increases bus-factor risk. Triplex model license (cc-by-nc-sa-4.0) may be restrictive for some commercial use cases. GitHub stars count varies between 7,193-7,668 across sources, suggesting rapid growth or measurement timing differences.
confidence.security_posture: Built-in user authentication with bcrypt password hashing, JWT access/refresh tokens, rate limiting for brute-force protection. Collections-based multitenancy for document-level access control. Configurable authentication requirement (can be toggled on/off). Supports Supabase as alternative auth provider. Email verification optional. Standard RAG attack surfaces apply: knowledge base poisoning, prompt injection through retrieved content, embedding inversion. No published security audit or SOC 2 compliance for self-hosted version. SciPhi Cloud enterprise includes dedicated support but compliance certifications not publicly documented. [uncertain]
